mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs for corporations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings slowdowns, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in housing starts signal weakening labor demand and consumer spending, jointly predicting negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with rising UNRATE and falling HOUST, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1400 thousand units during late-cycle expansions signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as retail sales and corporate earnings face headwinds.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle periods with HOUST < 1400, or Rank IC for regime-specific signal falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 110 index points indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output capacity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of INDPRO < 110 periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, triggering central bank tightening that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of CPIAUCSL (YoY) > 3.0% periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth above 3.0% indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as investor confidence strengthens.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of GDPC1 > 3.0% periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly employment growth below 100 thousand jobs signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending power and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days as earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of PAYEMS growth < 100 periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.
